title: Bounded prior-art source comparisons
scope_note: Passage-level attribution audit of two supplied completed comparisons; no theorem-correctness re-review, new mathematics, or comprehensive priority search.

cards.source: Lam and Leung, On Vanishing Sums of Roots of Unity
cards.source_type: Primary paper; earlier attribution reported by its authors
cards.locator: arXiv:math/9511209v1, Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4; PDF pp. 7–8
cards.exact_scope: Nonnegative vanishing sums of roots whose order has at most two prime divisors.
cards.finding: The prime-cycle cancellation input is classical. At squarefree order 3q, binary coefficients exclude mixing the two cycle directions, since such cycles intersect.
cards.caveat: This constrains pairwise support intersections; their sizes need not equal the matrix degree d. Original de Bruijn text was not independently inspected.

cards.source: Malikiosis and Kolountzakis, Fuglede’s conjecture on cyclic groups of order p^n q
cards.locator: arXiv:1612.01328v2, Theorem 1.2; Section 2 definition and Theorem 2.1; PDF pp. 2, 4
cards.exact_scope: One set A in Z_(p^n q), with equally many characters orthogonal on the same A; the primes are distinct.
cards.finding: Theorem 1.2 makes A a tile. For order 3q, this gives |A| dividing 3q. An arbitrary entry mask instead has pair-dependent intersection supports.
cards.caveat: Using this theorem for a mask degree d requires an additional extraction or structural reduction to a spectral set of size d. No such bridge was established in the inspected passages.

cards.source: Herr and Wiegand, Identifying complex Hadamard submatrices of the Fourier matrices via primitive sets
cards.locator: arXiv:1909.13145v4, Definition 1.1; Theorems 2.1 and 2.6; PDF pp. 2, 7, 10
cards.exact_scope: Complete selections of rows J and columns K, with |J|=|K|, retaining every entry in J × K.
cards.finding: The divisibility obstruction and primitive-set transfer theorem concern Cartesian Fourier submatrices, not arbitrary two-index zero patterns.
cards.caveat: A reduction from the arbitrary-mask problem is still needed. A counterexample at order 8 to universal block decomposition does not rule out a special order-3q reduction.

cards.source: Egan, A survey of complex generalized weighing matrices and a construction of quantum error-correcting codes
cards.source_type: Later survey with explicit construction; Berman attribution is secondary
cards.locator: arXiv:2309.07522v2, Definition 1.1; Example 3.5; Proposition 3.11; PDF pp. 2, 13, 18
cards.exact_scope: Zero or freely chosen k-th-root entries, satisfying WW*=wI; no entrywise Fourier-phase prescription.
cards.finding: The displayed CGW(5,4;3), taken in three direct-sum copies, gives CGW(15,4;15). Hence the unrestricted class admits weight 4 at order 15.
cards.caveat: This is a cited construction plus an elementary class comparison, not a new construction. It neither contradicts the fixed-phase theorem nor proves historical novelty. Berman’s original proof was not read.

cards.source: Atakishiyeva, Atakishiyev and Koornwinder, On a q-extension of Mehta’s eigenvectors of the finite Fourier transform for q a root of unity
cards.source_type: Primary paper; some historical orthogonality attribution is secondary
cards.exact_scope: Continuous q-Hermite H_n for general complex q; terminal degree N when q has exact order N.
cards.finding: H_N=2T_N and H_(kN+n)=(2T_N)^k H_n for 0≤n<N. For the target degrees below N, k=0 gives no lower-degree reduction.
cards.caveat: The finite orthogonality uses possibly complex weights. The source credits Zhedanov’s 1997 paper, whose full text remains unread; terminal simplicity does not establish all lower-degree simplicity.

cards.source: Spiridonov and Zhedanov, Zeros and orthogonality of the Askey-Wilson polynomials for q a root of unity
cards.exact_scope: Terminal degree N=ord(q), with E_N≠±2 and the nondegeneracy restrictions (2.9).
cards.finding: The degree-N formula gives its zeros; Theorem 1 gives finite orthogonality weights. The introduction expressly warns that complex recurrence coefficients do not guarantee simple zeros.
cards.caveat: Theorem 1 should not be labeled a theorem proving lower-degree simplicity. The q-Hermite limiting discussion does not close the lower-degree gap.

cards.source: Spiridonov and Zhedanov, q-Ultraspherical Polynomials for q a Root of Unity
cards.exact_scope: Recurrence coefficient (1−q^n)(1−q^(n+2β−1))/((1−q^(n+β))(1−q^(n+β−1))); positivity for specified real β and q=exp(2πi/N).
cards.finding: These positive-measure hypotheses differ from the continuous q-Hermite coefficient 1−q^n.
cards.caveat: The q-Hermite degeneration sends the multiplicative parameter q^β to zero, outside those real-β unit-circle ranges. No positivity-based simplicity conclusion transfers directly.

cards.source: Ismail and Witte, Discriminants and Functional Equations for Polynomials Orthogonal on the Unit Circle
cards.exact_scope: Rogers–Szegő normalized as R_n(q^(−1/2)z;q); the explicit product (5.17) is D(H_n,q).
cards.finding: The cited product uses the q-difference discriminant, not the ordinary derivative discriminant. Its nonvanishing cannot certify ordinary squarefreeness.
cards.caveat: The paper also discusses ordinary/generalized discriminants. Do not call the entire paper q-discriminant-only. Root-of-unity specialization of a product identity is an algebraic extension, not its original positive-measure hypothesis.

cards.source: Guàrdia, Montes and Nart, Newton polygons of higher order in algebraic number theory
cards.source_type: Primary paper; an exposition and development of classical Newton theory
cards.locator: arXiv:0807.2620v2, Section 1.1 degree definition; Section 1.2; Theorem 1.15 and Corollary 1.16; PDF pp. 3, 7, 11–12
cards.exact_scope: Finite extensions K/Q_p with v(K×)=Z; monic integral polynomials; φ=X for the ordinary polygon.
cards.finding: Once a side of length 2p and slope −(2p−1)/(2p) is proved, its side degree is one. Corollary 1.16 makes the corresponding factor irreducible.
cards.caveat: The source supplies this conditional implication, not the q-Hermite coefficient bounds establishing the side. Its higher-order separable-input algorithms must not be used circularly to assert squarefreeness.

cards.source: Dokchitser, Dokchitser, Maistret and Morgan, Arithmetic of hyperelliptic curves over local fields
cards.locator: Section 16, Definition 16.1; Theorem 16.2 first part; Lemmas 16.4–16.5
cards.exact_scope: Squarefree monic f defining y²=f over a local field of odd residue characteristic; applicable here to third-block degrees at least 6.
cards.finding: The proved root distances determine the discriminant valuation by established cluster bookkeeping. The curve discriminant is 16^g times the ordinary polynomial discriminant in the monic case, with equal valuations for odd p.
cards.caveat: Squarefreeness and the cluster picture are inputs. The first formula needs no semistability assumption. The separate minimal-model formula needs semistability and |k|>2g+1; it is not invoked.

cards.source_type: Author’s expository notes on a classical tool; not an originality source
cards.exact_scope: Polynomials integral over a complete nonarchimedean field; monicity is unnecessary.
cards.finding: A simple residual root gives its unique nearby lift after the integral normalization and residual equation have been established.
cards.caveat: This verifies the lifting tool only. The family-specific normalization and residual computation remain separate inputs; no priority is attributed to the notes.

unread_source_limits.source: Bond, Glickfield and Herr, On the existence of complex Hadamard submatrices of the Fourier matrices (2019)
unread_source_limits.basis: Antecedent and bibliographic entry checked in Herr–Wiegand. The earlier comparison recorded a full-text fetch failure.

unread_source_limits.source: Zhedanov, Gauss sums and orthogonal polynomials, International Journal of Modern Physics A 12 (1997), 289–294
unread_source_limits.basis: Reference [28] and complex-weight attribution checked in Atakishiyeva–Atakishiyev–Koornwinder.

unread_source_limits.source: Ismail, Difference equations and quantized discriminants for q-orthogonal polynomials (2003)
unread_source_limits.basis: Earlier comparison located the publisher abstract and recorded a full-text fetch error. No theorem-by-theorem exclusion is claimed.

publication_guards: Say no directly subsuming result was found in the inspected statements; do not say none exists.
Do not infer historical novelty from a hypothesis mismatch or a missing reduction.
Do not label Egan or Conrad as the original source of the classical result they present.
Keep terminal degree, lower degree, q-discriminant, ordinary discriminant, and minimal discriminant distinct.
Other adjacent sources from the supplied searches were not independently re-audited in this pass.
Public files contain original summaries and bibliographic links only, not full papers or private native-document data.
